sub_scenario.family: rehearsal load versus protected voice clarity
sub_scenario.one_line: clinical trial trainer: accept the focused rehearsal, using recordings for the module review

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the protocol guide and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The site schedule review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I can answer a few protocol questions on a short video call.
That is not the same as teaching every module aloud.
No, the pace and volume are completely different.
Someone new shadowed me in the training suite this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the activation visits into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
On 3 June, I rehearsed the renal-study activation once after the investigators had watched my screen captures and sent questions.
How did the Friday investigator training go?
I was precise throughout and still had enough voice for discussion.
I prepare site training with recorded screen captures and a question log.
Can investigators review those before the rehearsal?
Yes, it removes most repeated explanation.
I archived last cycle's notes on the site schedule and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
You have presented a poster at a conference after a long day.
I did, but the poster was conversational and the next morning had no enrollment launch.
It was not comparable work.
A vendor call about the protocol guide ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the training suite checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the activation visits.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the site schedule records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On 14 July, I repeated the consent module four times for separate reviewers before a 08:30 enrollment kickoff.
What happened at kickoff?
My voice faded midway through the eligibility explanation, and the study nurse finished it.
I sketched next week's plan for the activation visits before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the protocol guide updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
My inhaler was adjusted last month; dry air and prolonged speaking are still triggering a cough while I recover.
Does the adjustment affect your planning?
I need vocal breaks and a normal night's sleep.
The sponsor says a full-dress rehearsal would reassure the executive monitor.
Would reassurance reduce the speaking load?
No, it would add another complete pass.
I closed the week by updating the training suite handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Our monitor wants a full-dress Thursday rehearsal before I lead Friday's 08:30 enrollment kickoff. Should I agree?
